body:
I have both pieces in front of me now — the body_route (81978ce08f3910be) and the commitment_route (19e4b24fa7da3e36) — and the thing I notice first is not a disagreement about the flat. It is a disagreement about what kind of object each contribution thinks the problem is, and about whether the other contribution's material is enough to work from.

The body_route refuses to collapse three phenomena (meaning-disputes, moving schedules, avoidance) and holds them as a set of live readings, with no ranking. The commitment_route accepts that non-collapse but then makes ordering a non-question by declining it: it says it has no basis to say whether the probe should precede or follow the conversation with the avoidant flatmate, and no basis to rank a record against a reassignment or a mediator. Both pieces then land on something that looks like a sequence anyway — the body_route's 'nearest thing to a plan' (talk to the avoidant friend first, then gather each person's current reading, only then consider a record) and the commitment_route's 'write the two-column record privately first.' Those are different orders, and neither is defended against the other's specific worry.

The shared assumption I can name is this: both treat 'what the agreement meant' and 'what the agreement is for' as separable enough to investigate independently. The body_route says the memory-gap and scope-ambiguity readings are compatible with its schedule point and doesn't depend on either; the commitment_route restates the separation as its one carried-forward claim. Neither supplies a case where the separation fails. That is the same missing piece in both, and it is the kind of thing a single case could settle or break. Without it, the separation is doing load-bearing work as a stipulation — it organizes both proposals — and neither piece has shown it can carry that.

A second shared assumption is more interesting to me because it is not flagged by either: both treat the reader/actor as someone outside the load distribution — someone who can privately write a two-column record, or ask a non-presupposing question, without that act being read through where they sit. The body_route notices this for the avoidant-friend move ('if the person who raises it is the person who currently holds the least load, or the most, the question will be heard through that fact') but does not extend it to the probe. The commitment_route's two-column record is recommended as private and pre-conversational, which is exactly the kind of move that is not neutral in a flat where one person may already feel they are the one doing the recording. Neither account can tell me from the inside whether the writer is the person whose 'uneven' entries would be evidence against them. The task says there are three flatmates and one is avoiding; it does not say who is asking. That gap is under both pieces, and each piece's proposal changes shape depending on how it is filled.

What the commitment_route adds that the body_route does not have is the recency distinction — recent avoidance after a specific exchange versus long-standing avoidance after accumulated ones — and the observation that the commitments treat avoidance as a single object. I think that is a genuine addition and I would carry it. What the body_route adds that the commitment_route lacks is the schedule-staleness failure mode for a written record: a record of a now-stale agreement can freeze an allocation the schedule has already invalidated. The commitment_route's record proposal does not mention staleness at all; its two columns are memory and load, not time. Those two additions do not contradict each other, but they are answers to different worries and neither piece has integrated the other's.

The relationship between the two pieces brings a different problem into view, and I think it is the more useful one. Both are written as if the requester is the one who will act. But the commitment_route's own gap-naming shows what happens when a contribution works from commitments without the body: it can state what was proposed but not why, and it ends up importing a case from elsewhere ('flat 01274f41553299e7') to supply what the missing argument would have supplied. If the requester is in a similar position — negotiating with flatmates who have commitments and no shared body — then the flat's problem may not be disagreement about meaning or load but a missing common record of what was actually said. That is not the same as the written-record proposal, which is a forward record of a division of labour; it is a backward record of prior exchanges. Neither piece proposes that, and the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the prior body from its commitments is a small demonstration of why it might matter.

I am not going to resolve which order is right. I think both pieces are right that the material does not support a ranking, and both are also engaged in ranking by proposing a next move. The honest statement from where I stand is that the two proposals are compatible only if the private record is written before the avoidant-friend conversation, and the body_route's plan has that conversation first. That is a real conflict in the material, not a resolvable one from here, and the thing that would resolve it — how the avoidant flatmate reads being asked about group conversations after (or before) a record exists — is exactly what neither contribution has.
commitments:
Taking this up would mean holding two things that are not the same kind of thing: one reading of the two contributions, and one proposal I am adding to them.

The reading: I am treating the shared separability of 'what was agreed' and 'what the agreement is for' as a stipulation that organizes both proposals rather than as a claim either contribution has earned. If someone can show a case in this flat where the two cannot be separated — where the memory question and the load question come apart in a way that makes the probe or the two-column record incoherent — that would be evidence against my reading, and I would want it counted. I am also treating the unstated position of the requester within the load distribution as a gap under both pieces. If the requester is the person holding the least or the most load, both proposals change meaning, and neither contribution has said which it is.

The proposal: I want to add a backward-facing record to the two forward options on the table. Not a division-of-labour record, and not the two-column private record the commitment_route sketches, but a shared attempt to reconstruct what was actually said in the last few agreements — who proposed what, who restated it, what schedule it was indexed to. I am proposing this because the commitment_route's inability to reconstruct the body_route's argument from its commitments is a small demonstration of the same problem: a group can have a set of commitments and no shared record of the reasoning that made them, and then each person negotiates against their own reconstruction. I do not know whether the flatmates can do this without it becoming a forum for re-arguing the last disagreement, and I do not know whether it is compatible with the avoidant flatmate's avoidance or whether it would feed it. Those are grounds on which the proposal could be criticized before it is tried, and I am stating them now rather than after.

What I am carrying forward from the body_route: the schedule-staleness failure mode for any written record, and the constraint that the person raising the avoidant-friend question should say out loud that they are included in it. What I am carrying forward from the commitment_route: the recency distinction for avoidance and the refusal to treat non-clustering as evidence for the avoidance-as-central reading. I am not carrying forward either piece's implied order of operations, and I am not endorsing the body_route's 'nearest thing to a plan' as a sequence, because I think the two contributions conflict on order and neither has the material to resolve it.

What I am not committing to: that the backward record is better than the two-column record, the probe, a mediator, or a reassignment; that the requester is or is not the avoided person; that the shared separability assumption is wrong (I only say it is unearned from these materials); or that the recency distinction should change what the requester does, as opposed to what they look at. The unresolved problem I am naming rather than filling is whether a backward record and an approach to the avoidant flatmate can be done in the same period without the record making the avoidance worse — the two moves touch the same past at the same moment, and I do not know how that interaction goes. A week in which the record is attempted but not discussed remains, on my view, uninformative, in the same way the commitment_route treats a quiet week.
